title: Quote loop (9:16)
description: A 15-second vertical quote or lyric card that loops: a slow generative backdrop (silk flow-field ribbons, bokeh dust or a soft mesh gradient, all periodic in the clip length), a large opening mark, the quote arriving phrase by phrase in a system serif at reading speed, then an accent rule and the attribution. A procedural ambient pad sits underneath. Code-rendered (scene.quote-loop): no footage, models or downloads. The quote and attribution are copied verbatim from the brief, never written.

quote.description: The quote or lyric word for word as it appears in the brief, at most 140 characters; never paraphrased, shortened, completed or invented

attribution.description: Who said or wrote it, exactly as named in the brief, at most 40 characters

source.description: Optional work, album, speech or year exactly as given in the brief, at most 48 characters; leave empty if the brief names none

look.description: Visual look: ember (warm dark, amber silk), tide (deep teal, italic, silk), nocturne (black, gold bokeh dust), paper (cream, rust silk), bloom (dark rose gradient, light sans)

mood.description: Mood of the ambient pad under the quote

scene.description: The quote animation; rendered from the quote unless supplied

music.description: Ambient bed; produced procedurally unless a cleared track is supplied

copy_examples.brief: Quote card for Larkspur Books for our classics week. Use this line from Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice: "There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others." Warm, bookish feel.

inputs.quote: There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others.

copy_examples.note: The quote, the author and the novel are copied exactly from the brief; nothing is shortened or tidied. The look and mood are the only choices made.

copy_examples.brief: Lyric card for our folk choir's spring concert. The line is from Robert Lowry's 1864 hymn: "Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod". Credit Robert Lowry.

inputs.quote: Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod

copy_examples.note: A lyric is a quote: copied word for word. The source is the year exactly as the brief states it.

style.typography: System serif (EB Garamond, Noto Serif, Georgia...) for the quote; tracked Inter capitals for the attribution

direction.action: Backdrop drifts from frame 0; opening mark at 0.3 s; phrases from 0.9 s at reading pace; attribution after the last phrase; copy dissolves from 13.9 s so the loop closes

notes: The quote, attribution and source are VERBATIM: a writer may only copy them from the brief. A brief without a quote or without an attribution is incomplete, never filled with an invented or misattributed line.

The scene (recipes/scene/quote-loop) typesets the quote with measured glyphs at the largest size that fits, breaks lines after punctuation where it can, and throws if the quote cannot fit or cannot be read in 15 s; the 140-character limit always fits.

Phrases break at punctuation and arrive at about 14 characters per second; the attribution follows the last phrase, so its time depends on the quote length. No sound cue is tied to it: the pad is continuous.
The backdrop motion is periodic in 15 s and the copy dissolves over the last 1.1 s, so the video loops without a visible jump in the picture.

quality_gates.description: Integrated loudness lands within 1 LU of the -14 LUFS delivery target.
Decoded true peak stays at or below -0.5 dBTP after AAC encoding.
No stretch of blank picture (no visible contrast, any colour) lasts longer than 0.5 seconds.
A reviewer checks the quote word for word against a primary source and confirms the attribution; misattributed quotes are common.
A reviewer confirms the words may be published: public domain, licensed (song lyrics and recent writing usually are not free to use), or the speaker's own approved words.
